preconditions.description: The number of vertices n is an integer between 2 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a_i <= n for a_i in a)
preconditions.description: Each element a_i in the input sequence is an integer between 1 and n inclusive.
The input sequence a has exactly n elements.

postconditions.description: The minimum number of changes required to make the sequence valid is a non-negative integer.

postconditions.expression: is_valid_sequence(valid_sequence) and sum(1 for i in range(n) if valid_sequence[i] != a[i]) == min_changes
postconditions.description: The output sequence valid_sequence is valid (as defined by the task) and requires exactly min_changes modifications from the input sequence a.

postconditions.expression: not any(sum(1 for i in range(n) if candidate[i] != a[i]) < min_changes for candidate in valid_sequences) if valid_sequences else True
postconditions.description: There is no valid sequence achievable with fewer than min_changes modifications from the input sequence a.

invariants.expression: is_valid_sequence := (any(p_r == r for r in range(1, n + 1)) and all(has_path_to_root(p, r) for r in range(1, n + 1) if p[r - 1] == r) and len(set(p)) == n)
invariants.description: A sequence p is valid if and only if there exists exactly one root r (p[r-1] == r) and the graph formed by edges (i, p[i-1]) for all i is a tree (connected and acyclic). The helper has_path_to_root(p, r) checks if every node can reach the root r without cycles.

invariants.expression: has_path_to_root := lambda p, r: all(has_path(p, i, r) for i in range(1, n + 1))
invariants.description: For a given root r, every node i must have a path to r in the graph defined by p. The helper has_path(p, i, r) checks if there is a path from node i to root r.

invariants.expression: has_path := lambda p, i, r: (i == r) or (p[i - 1] != i and has_path(p, p[i - 1], r))
invariants.description: There is a path from node i to root r if either i is the root, or there is a path from p[i-1] to r and p[i-1] is not i (to avoid cycles).
